Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: the margin you want, the lowest price of a visit, the pay of a cleaner, the extra cost on pay, supplies and travel.
Check Services, Add-ons, Frequency Factors and Areas: these four small tables drive every quote. A labour hour is one cleaner working for one hour; the rate is what you charge for it.
Check Rate Card: the price, hours and cleaners for every service and size band. The price per m2, the price per labour hour and the margin fill in by themselves.
Enter every quote on Quotes. The hours, the price at the rate card, the discount, the margin, the monthly value and the follow-up check fill in by themselves. Open quotes with no follow-up turn red.
Use Site Visits, Office Quotes, Move-out Quotes and Post-construction Quotes for the jobs that need a measure or an estimate. A crew is the cleaners who work together on a job.
Write every follow-up on Quote Follow-ups and every reason a quote was lost on Lost Quotes. Read the price gap and the competitor type to decide where to be cheaper or not.
Keep Clients current. The rate card check shows who pays less than the rate card, and the review check shows who has not had a price review for 12 months.
Write every price change on Price Changes; the change in percent, the start date and the gain per month fill in. Send the letter from the printable documents.
Log market price checks and price tests. A price test is kept only if the win rate times the new price earns more than before.

Use the 14 calculators before you quote: area quote, room quote, frequency price, add-ons, office, move-out, post-construction, travel, minimum price, margin, discount limit, yearly increase, win rate and a what-if grid.
Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to open a chat with the text already written (28 messages).
A deep clean is a slow, detailed clean of every surface, and a rental turnover is the clean between two stays of a short-let rental; both have their own rate on Services.
Read the Quotes and Pricing Dashboard and Charts every week: win rate, open quotes, margin, price changes and quoted against actual hours.

One row per client with the crew, weekday and price of the visit; the next visit from the schedule, the days since the last visit, the visits per month and the visit check fill in by themselves.
Jobs by date, crew and cleaner

Recurring visits with the next visit
One row per client with a repeating plan, with the weekday, time and crew; the days between visits, the next visit, the visits and hours per month and an overdue check fill in by themselves.
Crew days with hours booked and hours free
One row per crew and day for the whole history and the weeks ahead, with the jobs, hours booked, revenue and road time; the hours free, the load and an overloaded check fill in by themselves.
One row per stop of a cleaner route with the minutes on the road and on site and the time the route leaves; the arrival and leave times of every stop fill in by themselves.
One row per visit moved to another day with the reason and who handled it; the days moved, the direction and the client phone fill in by themselves.
Skipped and cancelled visits with the fee
One row per visit that did not happen with the reason, the notice the client gave and the fee charged; the revenue lost, the notice check and the client phone fill in by themselves.
One-off bookings with the days to wait
One row per one-off clean (rental turnover, move-out, post-construction or deep clean) with the day asked, the day confirmed and the price; the days to wait and a quick or slow start check fill in.
Access and key notes by client
One row per client with the key type, the alarm, the parking, the pets and how the crew gets in; the area, the client phone and the phone of the usual cleaner fill in by themselves.
One row per client with products to avoid, rooms to skip, extra attention and the preferred time of day; the client phone and the phone of the team lead of their crew fill in by themselves.
The crews (the cleaners who work together on a job) with each member and the hours the member has each week; the day plan and the capacity tools read the total.
Areas with travel minutes and surcharge by zone
The four areas you serve, each in three zones (centre, middle, edge) with the minutes on the road and the surcharge added to a visit; the tools read the first row of each area, the centre.
The six services with the price per labour hour (one cleaner working for one hour) and the m2 one cleaner does in an hour; the duration and gap tools read these.
Holidays and closures with the visits to move
One row per holiday or closure with how it changes the schedule and how many visits fall on it; the days to the holiday and a move-now check fill in by themselves.
Waiting list of prospects by area
One row per prospect waiting for a slot with the area, frequency and preferred weekday; the days waiting and whether the wait is too long fill in by themselves.
The average jobs and labour hours of each crew on each weekday over the last 12 months against the hours the crew has that day; the load and the load check fill in by themselves.
Jobs and travel by area and weekday
The jobs and the minutes on the road in each area on each weekday over the last 12 months; the minutes per job show which days waste the most time on the road.
Visit confirmations and whether they came in time
One row per visit confirmation asked of the client with the day it was sent and the hours before the visit; the client, the visit date and whether it was confirmed in time fill in by themselves.
New clients with the days to the first visit
One row per new client with the day the quote was accepted and the day of the first visit; the days from quote to first visit and a quick or slow start check fill in by themselves.
